newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Immigration to Israel dips in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Immigration to Israel dips in 1996.

text.p: Immigration to Israel dropped by about eight percent in 1996 to 70,600, official figures showed on Monday.

Eighty-three percent of the immigrants arrived from republics of the former Soviet Union. The rest came from other parts of Europe, the United States, Argentina and other countries, the Central Bureau of Statistics said.
It said 16 percent of the newcomers listed their profession as engineer and 1.4 percent as doctor or dentist.

More than 780,000 Jews have immigrated to Israel since the former Soviet Union eased travel restrictions in 1989. The influx peaked in 1990 when nearly 200,000 immigrants arrived in the Jewish state and since 1992 the number has hovered between 70,000 and 80,000.
Israel has a population of about 5.5 million.
